title: Book One · Chapter 159: The Sign for Saturday
story:
Mr Qiu wants a sign for his customers. On River Street Day, he will close at one. He plans to come back a little after three. He plans to visit the school early in the afternoon. Then he will come back to sell things again.

“Are you sure?” Ronan asks.

“Will I close the table? Yes. About the exact minute? No. My legs may walk more slowly than the clock.”

Ronan may make the sign. Mr Qiu gives him the words to use first. CLOSED FOR A SHORT VISIT. BACK AFTER THREE. Beneath them they put the Saturday date.

Ronan wants to add the school name and a big arrow. Mr Qiu shakes his head. This sign is for his customers. They come here to buy pencils. They need his opening time. He is not inviting every customer to school.

“They may have work too,” he says.

Ronan makes the letters dark enough to read from the street. He does not fix the sign up yet. It is only Wednesday. Mr Qiu puts it under a board. It can stay flat there until Saturday.

Mrs Lan looks at it when she comes through the gate. “Is there a place to sit in the school room?” she asks. Ronan shows her the chair on his little plan.

“Not the repaired stool?” she asks.

“A chair too.”

“Good. I do not wish to test every repair in the street.”

Mr Qiu laughs. Mrs Lan's sister plans to visit her. If her sister comes later, Mrs Lan can visit the school first. She will decide that morning. Ronan leaves the question mark beside her name.

“Where is your stall now?” a customer asks. She has not been down this street since before the rain. Mr Qiu shows her the table and says he is working here now. He does not give the whole story unless she asks. She buys a book, checks its pages, and leaves smiling.

Ronan looks at the grey top. There are small marks from pencil boxes now. The dark foot is still dark. The old sign is still the old sign. He once wanted every part of the stall saved exactly as it was. Now he is used to seeing Mr Qiu here. He often walks past the table on his way home. He has stopped looking for it at the old stall.

A customer stops before they put the sign away. He reads it from the street side. He stands up straight and reads the hour easily. “Which Saturday?” he asks. Ronan makes the date a little larger. Mr Qiu asks the man to read it again. This time there is no second question. The man can read the date and time now. He understands the sign. Ronan puts the sign away with Mr Qiu.

At supper he tells Mum Mr Qiu will come early. She checks the stool-carrying time. They may walk to school together. Mr Qiu is kind and often helps. That does not mean he can carry everything.

“I know,” Ronan says.

He lists the pad and box under Mr Qiu's name. Then he adds a return tick beside each one. The pad and box are a loan. They must give both back after the display. Ronan writes that beside the return ticks.

Later Mr Qiu calls him to the gate. The old man has found a piece of stiff card. It can go behind the sign. It will not fold in the wind. Ronan helps fit it under the paper.

“Now the sign can stand,” Mr Qiu says.

Ronan looks at the square letters. “And you can leave for a while.”

Mr Qiu nods. He shuts the table at supper time. He locks the dry side space. Then he goes home with nothing to carry.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：loan＝借出的物品；stiff card＝硬纸板；back after three＝三点后回来。

情节提示：tick＝核对用的对勾；customer＝顾客；arrow＝箭头。

理解：1. Mr Qiu 的告示只需要告诉顾客什么？2. Mrs Lan 参加活动这件事是否已经确定？
